cohort: 3021 women giving birth to singleton infants in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, recruited from the All Our Babies study (started in 2008)
finding: After controlling for socio-demographic and labor and delivery characteristics, planned c-section was associated with early breastfeeding cessation.
mod_finding: Planned c-section was associated with early breastfeeding cessation, while women who delivered by emergency c-section had a higher proportion of breastfeeding difficulties compared to vaginal delivery or planned c-sections.
